messages.author: 4525396ad5bfc811
messages.subject: Problems with dirichlet_rng
parts:
Hello, 
I am trying to model the abundances of species in a community and then simulate those communities for the ultimate goal of calculating diversity estimates. I am running into trouble when using the dirichlet_rng function with out posterior estimates of alpha. Specifically, I am getting the following error:

Iteration:  1 / 100 [  1%]  (Warmup)Error : Invalid value of p1: model9f913abf015_simpleDivModel_v1_namespace::write_array(d): p1 is not a valid simplex. sum(p1) = nan, but should be 1
error occurred during calling the sampler; sampling not done.

This then leads to an error with the multinomial_rng because our probabilities are not valid simplexes: sum(Probabilites parameter) = nan, but should be 1.

I think this is because the dirichlet_rng function generates Dirichlet variates with prior counts plus one alpha, which is different from what dirichlet(alpha) is doing? 

Is there a way around this or an alternative parameterization that would accomplish what we want?

Here is my model thus far, along with both the model and r scripts/data as attachments. 

Thank you for any help or advice you might have!

Zach Marion

data{

int<lower=1> samps; # number of samples

int<lower=1> spp; # number of species

int<lower=0> y[samps, spp]; # species abundances

vector[spp] alpha0; # Hyperpriors for dirichlet alphas

int<lower=1> sizes[samps]; # number of individuals observed in each sample

}


parameters{

simplex[spp] theta[samps]; # quadrat-specific category proportions

simplex[spp] a; # spp proportions multiplied by varm

real<lower=1e-5, upper=1000> varm; # dirichlet concentration param.

real<lower=min(sizes), upper=max(sizes)> Nmu; # negbinom mean 

real<lower=1e-6, upper=1000> Nphi; # negbiom overdispersion

}


transformed parameters{

vector[spp] alpha; # dirichlet alphas with dirichlet hyperpriors

alpha <- a * varm + machine_precision(); # ensures alphas > 0

}


model{

a ~ dirichlet(alpha0);

for(i in 1:samps){

theta[i] ~ dirichlet(alpha);

y[i] ~ multinomial(theta[i]);

sizes[i] ~ neg_binomial_2(Nmu, Nphi);

}

}


generated quantities{

# for a random pair of hypothetical samples 

simplex[spp] p1; # "true" relative abundances

simplex[spp] p2;

int<lower=0> N1; # no. ind. for 'posterior pred.' diversity estimates

int<lower=0> N2;

int<lower=0> x1[spp]; # random hypothetical communities

int<lower=0> x2[spp];


# generate 'true' relative abundances

p1 <- dirichlet_rng(alpha);

p2 <- dirichlet_rng(alpha);

# generate random number of indiv. while ensuring N1 & N2 > 0

N1 <- 0;

N2 <- 0;

while(N1==0){

N1 <- neg_binomial_2_rng(Nmu, Nphi);

}

while(N2==0){

N2 <- neg_binomial_2_rng(Nmu, Nphi);

}

# generate random multinomial species counts

# x1 <- multinomial_rng(p1, N1);

# x2 <- multinomial_rng(p2, N2);

}

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Problems with dirichlet_rng
parts:
Thanks, definitely a bug. I submitted an issue:

https://github.com/stan-dev/stan/issues/1474

which I'll summarize here.

I managed to recreate a version of your problem with a little test
program:

parameters {
vector<lower=0>[5] alpha;
}
model {
alpha ~ normal(0, 0.0001);
}
generated quantities {
simplex[5] beta;
beta <- dirichlet_rng(alpha);
}

and here's what I get in RStan 2.6.0:

-----------------------------------
> fit <- stan('dir_rand.stan')

TRANSLATING MODEL 'dir_rand' FROM Stan CODE TO C++ CODE NOW.
COMPILING THE C++ CODE FOR MODEL 'dir_rand' NOW.

SAMPLING FOR MODEL 'dir_rand' NOW (CHAIN 1).

Iteration: 1 / 2000 [ 0%] (Warmup)Error : Invalid value of beta: modele264fa804e_dir_rand_namespace::write_array(d): beta is not a valid simplex. sum(beta) = nan, but should be 1
error occurred during calling the sampler; sampling not done

-------------------------------

The worst part is that errors in generated quantities just kill the whole
process because there's no recovery possible (it's too late to reject a
sample and we don't want feedback from generated quantities anyway).

The problem is that everything's under or overflowing internally and we're
getting draws like this:

iterations [,1] [,2] [,3] [,4] [,5]
[1,] NaN NaN NaN NaN NaN
[2,] 0 1 0 0 0
[3,] NaN NaN NaN NaN NaN
[4,] NaN NaN NaN NaN NaN
[5,] NaN NaN NaN NaN NaN
[6,] NaN NaN NaN NaN NaN
>

So you can't even solve the problem by relaxing the declaration of the simplex.

I'll try to fix it by scaling the RNG draws internally, but it won't land
before the 2.7.0 we're working on getting out the door right this second.

- Bob

P.S. The Dirichlet (and Beta) is traditionally parameterized
with "prior counts" plus 1 and this is always what's used in Stan.
For example, Dirichlet({1,1,1,1}) is uniform over 4-simplexes and
the mean of Beta(2,3) is 1/3 (The (2,3) parameters corresponding to 1
prior success and 2 prior failures).

messages.author: 3f22b207863d2049
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Problems with dirichlet_rng
parts:
You could temporarily circumvent the problem by generating Dirichlet variates by means of gamma-distributions as follows:

x_1 <- gamma_rng(a_1, 1);
x_2 <- gamma_rng(a_2, 1);
x_3 <- gamma_rng(a_3, 1);
...
x_n <- gamma_rng(a_n, 1);

// build simplex in pseudo-code:
probs <- c(x_1, x_2, x_3, x_4) / sum(x_1, x_2, x_3, x_4)  // implies probs ~ dirichlet(a_1, a_2, a_3, ..., a_n)

See also http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dirichlet_distribution#Gamma_distribution

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Problems with dirichlet_rng
parts:
That's how we're currently generating Dirichlet variates.
The problem is that when alpha = 1e-5, most of the probabilty
mass of gamma(alpha, 1) is for values so small that they underflow
to 0 in practice when using double-precision arithmetic.

So what I'm working on in the way of fix is to use the technique
from this paper:

G. Marsaglia and W. Tsang. A simple method for generating
gamma variables. ACM Transactions on Mathematical Software, 26(3):363-372, 2000.

http://dl.acm.org/citation.cfm?id=358414

as discussed here:

http://www.hongliangjie.com/2012/12/19/how-to-generate-gamma-random-variables/

That lets me generate a gamma (P)RNG x ~ gamma(alpha, 1) as:

x_raw[i] = gamma_rng(1 + alpha[i], 1); // now first arg > 0
u[i] = uniform_rng(0, 1);

x[i] = x_raw * pow(u[i], 1 / alpha[i]);

Then I just do all the fussy work that might underflow on the log scale,
so that

log_x[i] = log(x_raw[i]) + log(u[i]) / alpha[i];

Then I generate the denominator

log_sum_x = log_sum_exp(log_x),

which is numerically stable, then generate

log_theta[i] = log_x[i] - log_sum_x

and then take

theta[i] = exp(log_theta[i])

at which point we get mostly underflow to 0 because of the way Dirichlet works,
but that's the best we can do without returning results on the log scale, that is
returning log(theta) where theta ~ dirichleta(alpha).

It's testing now, but it seems to work OK.

- Bob

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Problems with dirichlet_rng
parts:
It's an edge case. With the fix, what you're going to
get is that each draw will have a 1 in one position and
zeroes elsewhere. This comes from overflow/underflow issues
with using double-precision floating point.

I can see the draws on the log scale and they're around 10^30
different from each other, so there's no way to squeeze that
into a double on the linear scale.

This may mean that your model isn't doing what you think
it's doing if you're getting Dirichlet parameters << 1.

- Bob
